note: Method cards: what the organisation knows about trading-research methods, where each came from, how we test it and what our own data said. Agents read these (R&D's idea invention gets every lesson). Results are on seen history and can change as data grows; the scout re-tests every cycle. Ideas from other projects were rewritten, never copied.

cards.idea: A decision made on day i must not change when every later day is removed; if it does, the rule is using the future.
cards.howWeTest: research_checks.check_rules on 6 decision days for every scout idea; an idea that fails cannot pass.
cards.result: No catalogue idea uses the future (20 Oct 2026).
cards.lesson: Every new rule must survive the lookahead check before its backtest means anything.

cards.idea: A decision should not depend on how far back the data starts.
cards.howWeTest: The same decision with only the last 300 sessions; a difference is reported as warmupSensitive.
cards.result: No catalogue idea is sensitive at the sampled days.
cards.lesson: Prefer fixed look-back windows to quantities measured from the first day of the data.

cards.idea: Trying many ideas on the same history finds lucky ones; the bar must rise with every idea tried.
cards.howWeTest: Sign test against the basket at 0.05 divided by every idea ever tried (Bonferroni), and ahead in both halves.
cards.result: 17 ideas, bar 0.0029: none passes on 10 years of the 8 shares or on 37 NIFTY 50 shares.
cards.lesson: Propose few, genuinely different ideas; each one makes every idea harder to pass.

cards.idea: Choose the best idea on the past three years, hold it for the next year, repeat; judge only the held years.
cards.howWeTest: research_checks.walk_forward over every scout idea.
cards.result: Picking the best past idea LOST out of sample: 8 shares 33 ahead / 37 behind months, -0.35% a month; NIFTY 50 35/35, -0.32% a month.
cards.lesson: The best backtest is not a good choice by itself: past winners among these ideas did not keep winning.

cards.idea: An edge must beat random pickers that hold the same number of shares and pay the same costs.
cards.howWeTest: 100 random 3-share pickers per scout run; every idea gets beatsRandomPct.
cards.result: 8 shares: random pickers trail the basket by a median 0.16% a month (costs). Momentum 6m top 3 beats 81% of them.
cards.lesson: Compare with random pickers, not only with cash: costs alone make most active rules trail the basket.

cards.idea: Judge risk as well as return: Sharpe, Sortino, maximum drawdown and its length, Calmar, profit factor, expectancy, SQN.
cards.howWeTest: research_checks.stats on every scout idea and on the basket.
cards.result: 8-share basket: 13.6% a year, Sharpe 0.79, worst fall -35%. The 200-day trend filter: 12.95% a year, Sharpe 0.95, worst fall -12.7%, uninvested cash earning nothing.
cards.lesson: The scout's pass test counts months ahead on return only, so it cannot see a rule whose value is lower risk; the trend filter is the clearest case.

cards.idea: Today's index members over past years leave out the companies that fell out, flattering every backtest.
cards.howWeTest: Not removable with free data; every NIFTY 50 result is labelled research-only.
cards.result: Reversal 1m bottom 3 looks strong on NIFTY 50 (63/43 months, +0.56% a month, p 0.032) but losers that later dropped out are missing.
cards.lesson: Never trust a reversal or value result on today's members; it needs point-in-time membership before it counts.

cards.source: our cost model (STT, stamp, exchange, SEBI, GST, DP charge, slippage)
cards.idea: Every unit of turnover costs about 0.15% one way; high-turnover rules pay it every month.
cards.howWeTest: Scout returns are net of turnover cost; fills in paper trading pay the real fee model.
cards.result: Monthly 3-share rules lose about 0.16% a month to the basket on average just from trading.
cards.lesson: An idea must earn more than its turnover costs; favour rules that change holdings rarely.

cards.idea: A small edge in a noisy monthly record takes a very long time to prove: n = ((z_bar + z_power) x noise / edge)^2 months.
cards.howWeTest: research_checks.months_to_prove for every scout idea, at the scout's Bonferroni bar and 80% power.
cards.result: On the 8 shares the best idea would need about 640 years of records; momentum 6m top 3 far longer. On 37 NIFTY 50 shares the best (reversal) about 70 years.
cards.lesson: With 8 similar shares and one decision a month, skill cannot be proven in a lifetime; more independent bets (a wider universe, more uncorrelated strategies) are needed before anything can be proven.

cards.source: Indian capital-gains tax (short-term 20%, long-term 12.5% since 23 Jul 2024); our scout
cards.idea: A rule that sells often pays short-term tax every year; holding pays long-term tax once, at the end.
cards.howWeTest: research_checks.after_tax_cagr: the share sold each year (half the turnover) pays short-term tax on that year's gain, the rest long-term at the end. An approximation.
cards.result: 8 shares: the basket keeps 12.5% a year after tax; the momentum bot's rule keeps 9.8% monthly (52% turnover), 10.7% quarterly and 12.3% yearly (10.5% turnover, sales assumed after 12 months). No idea beats the basket after tax. NIFTY 50: basket 15.7%, yearly momentum 10.4%.
cards.lesson: After tax, monthly rebalancing among these shares loses to holding them; trading once a year recovers most of the loss but still only matches the basket. Low turnover is worth more than a clever signal.

cards.idea: Hold the shares that rose most over the last months.
cards.howWeTest: Scout families momentum 3/6/12 months, top 2-4.
cards.result: 8 shares, 106 months: 6m top 3 ahead 61/45 months but 0.00% a month on average, Sharpe 0.66 vs basket 0.79, worst fall -42%. NIFTY 50: negative.
cards.lesson: Momentum on these shares adds risk without adding return; the live momentum bot is an experiment, not a proven edge.

cards.idea: Hold the basket while it is above its 200-day average, else cash.
cards.howWeTest: Scout idea trend-filter-200d; family filter trend-200d.
cards.result: Lower return than the basket in most differing months, but far smaller falls (-12.7% vs -35%, mostly the 2020 crash) and the best Sharpe (0.95 vs 0.79). The risk lens finds the Sharpe gain not significant (better in 63% of bootstrap samples, p 0.37). With an assumed 6% on cash it would earn 14.2% a year against the basket's 13.6%.
cards.lesson: Use trend as a RISK tool (size and protection), not as a return-beating rule; its edge on risk is plausible but not proven.

cards.source: block bootstrap of Sharpe ratios; standard practice
cards.idea: Judge an idea on risk too: is its Sharpe really above the basket's, and is its worst fall smaller?
cards.howWeTest: Circular block bootstrap (6-month blocks, 1000 samples) of paired monthly returns, at the same Bonferroni bar; plus worst fall and an assumed 6% cash yield. Report only.
cards.result: No idea would pass on risk either, on the 8 shares or on 37 NIFTY 50 shares (best: trend filter, p 0.37).
cards.lesson: A smaller worst fall in one history is one event, not a proven skill; a risk case needs the same evidence bar as a return case.

cards.idea: Falls on rising volume signal institutional selling; many in 25 sessions mean risk.
cards.howWeTest: market_regime.py study on 10 years; scout idea equal-weight-distribution.
cards.result: After SEVERE days the basket fell further (-3.58% vs -2.04% worst fall in 20 sessions) and earned less; as a cash filter it lost return but cut the worst fall to -9%.
cards.lesson: The regime is a useful warning; it does not time entries and exits for profit.

cards.idea: Hold shares in strong uptrends near their 52-week highs.
cards.howWeTest: Scout idea trend-template-25pct-top3.
cards.result: 8 shares: -0.63% a month against the basket over 106 months.
cards.lesson: Breakout-style selection did not work on large Indian caps at a monthly rebalance.

cards.idea: Buy oversold shares (low RSI) that are still above their 200-day average.
cards.howWeTest: Scout idea pullback-rsi40-top3.
cards.result: 8 shares: -0.95% a month against the basket.
cards.lesson: Buying dips in uptrends, held for a month, lost to simply holding.

cards.source: multi-factor investing practice; NSE factor indices
cards.idea: Rank shares on several weak signals at once (momentum, calm, consistency) and hold the best average.
cards.howWeTest: Scout family combo; catalogue idea combo-6m-60d-top3.
cards.result: 8 shares: -0.04% a month against the basket; NIFTY 50 (37 shares): -0.44% a month, with 51-91% monthly turnover.
cards.lesson: Combining price signals did not help on these large caps at a monthly rebalance; factor premiums need a broad universe, slower rebalancing and, for quality and value, fundamentals.

cards.source: QuantConnect Lean algorithm framework (Apache-2.0, idea only)
cards.idea: Separate universe selection, alpha (insights with direction and horizon), portfolio construction, execution and risk management; each stage is replaceable and scored on its own.
cards.howWeTest: Our organisation already separates these: universe (datasets), alpha (bots' proposals), review (signal-risk-v2), execution (eod_trader), risk (limits, halt, regime advice).
cards.result: Mapped; scored insights correspond to our outcome scoring.
cards.lesson: When adding a member, say which stage it serves and score it at that stage.

cards.idea: The same code should decide in research and in live paper trading, with deterministic, reproducible runs; live adds timing and reconciliation the simulation lacks.
cards.howWeTest: Release fingerprints: a bot trades only while its exact code is the authorised release; forward tests are pre-registered.
cards.result: In place for the rule bot and R&D bots.
cards.lesson: Never let a researched rule and a trading rule drift apart; a changed file needs a new release.

cards.idea: Automatic brakes: stop new trades after a run of losses, after a drawdown, or for a cooldown after an exit.
cards.howWeTest: Our equivalents: realised-loss limit and halt, management review suspensions, live fitness and rollback.
cards.result: Covered by existing controls; brakes that change limits stay with the owner.
cards.lesson: Prefer a brake that pauses a bot over one that changes money or limits.

cards.idea: Several personas rehearse how a world story plays out for the shares.
cards.howWeTest: Shadow calls scored after 5 sessions against the basket, per persona.
cards.result: Not yet run (needs the local model).
cards.lesson: A perspective earns trust only through its scored record.
